relevance_reason: The title reports an inherited TOP2B mutation and suggests mutational hotspots in the TOPRIM domain, which bears on the TOP2B-related BILU/Hoffman syndrome. Only the title was available, so no patient or variant details can be extracted.

findings.statement: Erdős et al. (2021) reported an inherited TOP2B mutation and suggested that it might confirm mutational hotspots in the TOPRIM domain of TOP2B.
quotes: Inherited TOP2B Mutation: Possible Confirmation of Mutational Hotspots in the TOPRIM Domain.

relevance_reason: Identifies the TOP2B A485P mutation as the cause of BILU syndrome in two families. Also includes functional studies and bone marrow phenotyping.

findings.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) studied 2 previously described unrelated families with autosomal dominant BILU syndrome (B-cell immunodeficiency, limb anomalies, and urogenital malformations), one from Cyprus (family A) and one from France (family B). The patients had absent or reduced B cells but normal T and myeloid cells.
quotes: The autosomal dominant syndrome of unknown etiology called BILU (B-cell Immunodeficiency, Limb anomalies and Urogenital malformations) was previously described in two unrelated families originating from Cyprus and France
The BILU patients have absent or reduced B cells but normal T and myeloid cells

findings.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) performed multicolor flow cytometry on a bone marrow aspirate from BILU patient II:4 of family A and found complete absence of any CD19+ cells, including pro-B, pre-B, immature, and mature B cells, with normal T, NK, and myeloid lineages, indicating a block at the earliest stages of B-cell development after the common lymphoid progenitor stage. The block was described as leaky, since immunoglobulins and small numbers of B cells were found in peripheral blood of several patients.
quotes: found a complete absence of any CD19+ cells, including pro-B, pre-B, immature and mature B cells, but normal T, NK and myeloid cell lineages
This finding for the first time shows that TOP2B is critical during the earliest stages of B cell lineage after the Common Lymphoid Progenitor (CLP) stage
Nevertheless, in TOP2B deficiency this block is leaky, because immunoglobulins and small numbers of B cells have been found in peripheral blood of several patients

findings.statement: In family A with BILU syndrome, Papapietro et al. (2020) used exome sequencing of 4 family members to identify a de novo heterozygous c.1453G>C mutation in the TOP2B gene, resulting in an ala485-to-pro (A485P) substitution. The mutation arose de novo in affected II:4 and was transmitted to her affected daughter. Sanger sequencing found the same mutation in patients of family B. The mutation was absent from more than 90,000 subjects in gnomAD. It affected an alanine conserved in eukaryotic and prokaryotic type II topoisomerases and was predicted to destabilize an alpha helix in the catalytic TOPRIM domain.
quotes: This heterozygous G>C mutation at the cDNA nucleotide 1,453 of the TOP2B gene (ENST00000435706) resulted in the alanine to proline substitution at position 485 (A485P) of topoisomerase 2β (TOP2B).
appeared de novo in their affected daughter II:4 and then was transmitted to her affected daughter III:1
we used Sanger sequencing and found that exactly the same mutation was present in patients of family B

findings.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) found reduced TOP2B protein in patient T cells, fibroblasts, and iPSCs. In TOP2B-knockout HEK293 cells, the A485P mutant showed a degradation product, suggesting it was less stable, but it still interacted with TOP2A. Purified recombinant A485P protein had more than 10-fold reduced DNA relaxation and decatenation activity. Patient T-cell blast lysates had reduced decatenation activity.
quotes: found reduced amounts of the TOP2B protein in patients’ cells in comparison to cells of healthy controls
We found that enzymatic activities of TOP2BA485P were reduced more than 10 fold
The decatenation activity of lysed patient’s T cell blasts was reduced

findings.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) found that expressing TOP2B A485P in wildtype HEK293 cells, or co-expressing it with wildtype TOP2B in knockout cells, lowered decatenation activity compared with wildtype alone. They concluded that the mutant has a dominant-negative effect on wildtype TOP2B and TOP2A rather than causing haploinsufficiency. They noted that gnomAD contains 42 unaffected individuals with heterozygous loss-of-function TOP2B variants.
quotes: These results indicate that mutant TOP2BA485P protein not only itself has reduced intrinsic enzymatic activity, but also exerts a dominant negative effect on the activities of wild-type TOP2B and TOP2A.

haploinsufficiency of TOP2B is an unlikely causative mechanism of BILU because multiple subjects with various heterozygous loss-of-function TOP2B mutations have been detected in population cohorts (e.g. the gnomAD database has 42 such unaffected subjects

findings.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) noted that other dominant TOP2B mutations in the TOPRIM domain cause Hoffman syndrome (B-cell deficiency, limb abnormalities, and facial dysmorphism). They concluded that BILU and Hoffman syndromes are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.
quotes: Our results indicate that BILU and Hoffman syndromes are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.

relevance_reason: The paper identifies heterozygous TOP2B mutations as the cause of the syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency (Hoffman/BILU syndrome) in three families and characterizes the phenotype and mechanism with yeast and mouse models.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) reported that sequencing of patients with B cell-restricted immunodeficiency revealed autosomal dominant mutations in TOP2B, which encodes a type II topoisomerase required to alleviate topological stress during DNA replication and gene transcription; they stated that their findings define a class of B-cell immunodeficiency and were the first description of a defined monogenic syndrome due to mutations in the essential gene TOP2B.
quotes: Sequencing of patients with B cell-restricted immunodeficiency reveals autosomal dominant mutations in TOP2B. TOP2B encodes a type II topoisomerase, an essential gene required to alleviate topological stress during DNA replication and gene transcription, with no previously known role in B cell development.
Thus, our findings define a class of B-cell immunodeficiency and are the first description of a defined monogenic syndrome due to mutations in the essential gene TOP2B.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) noted that the syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency with facial dysmorphism and limb anomalies previously described in two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inheritance had subsequently been named Hoffman syndrome, with the genetic etiology unknown until their study.
quotes: We previously described two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology,. While agammaglobulinemia and hypogammaglobulinemia are common to several classic immunodeficiencies, the patients were also affected by facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies, identifying this as a unique syndrome, subsequently named Hoffman syndrome, but the genetic etiology remained unknown until now.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) restudied two previously reported unrelated families with autosomal dominant syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency; the probands from each family presented with recurrent infections by polysaccharide-encapsulated bacteria, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent CD19+ B cells, but had normal T-cell responses to mitogens. A third patient, initially reported as having an atypical presentation of Ablepharon-Macrostomia syndrome, was later found to have humoral immunodeficiency.
quotes: The probands from each family presented with recurrent infections by polysaccharide-encapsulated bacteria, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent CD19+ B cells, but had normal T-cell responses to mitogens.
A third patient initially being reported as having an atypical presentation of Ablepharon-Macrostomia syndrome, was later found to have humoral immunodeficiency.

phenotypes.text: normal T-cell proliferative response to mitogens

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) tabulated immunologic laboratory values at diagnosis in 4 patients from 3 families (ages at presentation 7 years, 35 years, 6 years, and 5 years), showing absent or markedly reduced CD19+ B cells (0, 48, 0, and 0 cells/microliter), low total IgG (232, 631, 73, and 242 mg/dL), deficient or undetectable tetanus, diphtheria and H. influenzae B titers, normal CD3+, CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts, and normal mitogen stimulation; reduced CD16+ NK cell numbers were present in two patients.
quotes: CD19+ B cells (cells/μL) | 0 | 48 | 0 | 0
Mitogen stimulation | normal | normal | normal | normal
The reduced numbers of NK cells in two of the patients (Table 1) may be consequent to similar binding patterns of Top2b to the Nfil3 promoter, a regulator of NK cell differentiation–.

phenotypes.text: absent or reduced circulating CD19+ B cells

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) reported that Hoffman syndrome patients had no detectable B cells in the peripheral blood and did not form germinal centers, and did not generate protective serologic titers to immunization; however, detectable amounts of circulating immunoglobulins indicated that some B cells were present but below the clinical limits of detection, while numbers of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes and T-cell mitogen stimulation were normal. No malignancy was observed in the patients or mice.
quotes: Hoffman syndrome patients have no detectable B cells in the peripheral blood, nor form germinal centers, and patients did not generate protective serologic titers to immunization; however, detectable amounts of circulating immunoglobulins indicate that some B cells are present, but are below the clinical limits of detection.
While these recombination defects can lead to immunodeficiency,, we might expect a greater tendency to malignancy, which has not been observed in our patients or mice.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Absence of lymph node germinal center

phenotypes.text: failure to generate protective titers to immunization

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) performed whole genome sequencing of affected and unaffected persons in two unrelated families with autosomal dominant syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency, filtering for novel, dominantly inherited coding variants, and identified TOP2B as the only gene with nonsynonymous changes in only the affected patients in both families; in family 1 a heterozygous missense mutation c.1448C>T, p.S483L was found and in family 2 a de novo in-frame deletion c.1761_1763delAGA, p.EE587E. All mutations were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and affected the TOPRIM (DNA gating) domain and highly conserved amino acids; TOP2B had a probability of loss-of-function intolerance (pLI) of 1.
quotes: One gene, TOP2B, which encodes topoisomerase IIβ, was affected by a heterozygous variant in each family: a de novo in-frame deletion c.1761_1763delAGA, p.EE587E, and a missense mutation c.1448C > T, p.S483L.
After applying the filters to select for a causal variant, there was only 1 gene with nonsynonymous changes in only the affected patients in both families, TOP2B (Fig. 1a).

Notably, TOP2B has a probability of loss of function intolerance (pLI) of 1 (Supplementary Table 5), similar to most known severe haploinsufficiency human disease genes, suggesting that the identified heterozygous mutations in our patients could cause disease either through haploinsufficiency or a partial genetic dominance.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) found, by independent reanalysis of clinical whole-exome sequencing in a third patient (family 3) initially reported as atypical Ablepharon-Macrostomia syndrome and later found to have humoral immunodeficiency, a heterozygous TOP2B variant c.1897G>A, p.G633S, which was absent from the 1000 Genomes Project, ESP6500SI, ExAC v0.3, and their in-house exome variant database, and was confirmed by Sanger sequencing; like the other mutations it affected the TOPRIM domain of TOP2B.
quotes: Independent reanalysis of clinical whole-exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous TOP2B variant: c.1897G > A, p.G633S. All of the mutations affected the TOPRIM domain of TOP2B (Fig. 1b).

Therefore, we selected for variants not present in 1000 Genomes Project, ESP6500SI, ExAC v0.3, and not identified in subjects by our in-house exome variant database. A variant in TOP2B was identified as the most likely candidate.
For all three families, mutations in TOP2B were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) showed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that chimeric yeast–human TOP2B constructs or yeast ScTOP2 vectors carrying the patient mutations S483L, EE587E, or G633S failed to complement the temperature-sensitive top2-4 allele at the nonpermissive temperature and did not allow recovery of top2-delta haploid spore clones, indicating that each patient mutation disrupts topoisomerase II function.
quotes: Similar to the mutant chimeric constructs but unlike the wild-type ScTOP2 plasmid, the mutant ScTOP2-S483L, -EE587E, and -G633S vectors were unable to complement the top2–4 at the nonpermissive temperature, consistent with a loss of function (Fig. 2a).

No haploid spore clones lacking TOP2 were recovered with an empty vector control or with the ScTOP2-EE587E, -S483L, or -G633S vectors (Fig. 2b). Taken together, these results indicate that each of our patient mutations disrupt topoisomerase II function.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) demonstrated that yeast strains carrying one wild-type and one mutant copy of TOP2 (ScTOP2-EE587E or -S483L) grew more slowly than wild-type controls and that nuclear fractions from strains with the mutant alleles decatenated kinetoplast DNA less effectively than fractions containing a single wild-type copy, indicating that the disease-associated versions of TOP2 have a partial dominant negative phenotype.
quotes: Growth analysis demonstrated that the strains with ScTOP2-EE587E or ScTOP2-S483L grew more slowly than the wild-type controls (Fig. 2c), but were not associated with the activation of the DNA damage checkpoint (Supplementary Fig. 4b).

Remarkably, fractions from the strain with only one copy of wild-type TOP2 decatenated kinetoplast DNA more effectively than fractions from strains with one wild-type and one mutant copy of TOP2 (Fig. 2d, Supplementary Fig. 4c). Thus, the disease-associated versions of TOP2 have a partial dominant negative phenotype in S. cerevisiae based on growth and/or decatenation assays.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) found that because Top2b-null mice do not survive the perinatal period, they bred Top2b-flox2 mice to cd19-cre and mb1-cre lines; Top2b-/-mb1-cre and Top2b-/-cd19-cre mice had fewer peripheral blood CD19+ B cells than wild-type littermates, with altered splenic follicle structure, reduced marginal zone and follicular B-cell zones, fewer PrePro B, Pre B and immature B cells in bone marrow, fewer splenic B cells at every developmental stage, reduced kappa-deleting recombination excision circles, and significantly reduced Pax5 with unchanged Rag1 expression.
quotes: Flow cytometry of peripheral blood demonstrated that Top2b−/−mb1-cre and Top2b−/−cd19-cre mice had fewer CD19+ B cells than wild-type controls (Fig. 3a, Supplementary Fig. 5a).

Immunophenotyping demonstrated that the bone marrow of Top2b−/−mb1-cre mice have fewer PrePro B cells, Pre B, and immature B cells compared to control mice (Fig. 3K). In the spleen, there were fewer B cells at every developmental stage compared to control mice (Fig. 3l).

Furthermore, expression of Pax5, a B-cell specific transcription factor expressed at most stages of B-cell development–, was significantly reduced in B cells derived from Top2b−/−mb1-cre mice while Rag1 expression was unchanged (Fig. 3n, o).

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) showed that Top2b-/-mb1-cre mice failed to produce ovalbumin-specific IgG after immunization and had impaired anti-Pneumovax-23 IgG3 and significantly reduced IgG2b responses, while PPV23-specific IgM and B-1 cells were unaffected; in vitro, LPS-stimulated Top2b-deficient B cells failed to proliferate, showed increased cell death by LDH release, and had less robust upregulation of MHC II, consistent with the failure to mount a vaccine response observed in patients.
quotes: Fourteen days after immunization, serum samples from control mice demonstrated increased OVA-specific IgG, which was not observed in Top2b−/−mb1-cre mice (Fig. 4a).

Similar to OVA immunization, anti-PPV23 IgG3 trended downwards, and anti-PPV23 IgG2b was significantly reduced in Top2b−/−mb1-cre mice compared to controls at 6 weeks post-immunization (Fig. 4c, d). The immunization responses in the Top2b−/−mb1-cre mice are consistent with the failure to mount a vaccine response observed in patients.

After 72 h of stimulation, Top2b−/− mb1-cre derived B cells failed to proliferate and had increased cell death compared to their wild-type counterparts (Fig. 4e–g). In addition, surviving Top2b−/− mb1-cre B cells had less robust upregulation of the activation marker MHC II (Fig. 4h).

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) generated a constitutive knockin mouse carrying the murine equivalent of the patient TOP2B EE587E mutation; Top2bEE587E/EE587E homozygotes were not viable, as for Top2b-/- mice, whereas Top2b+/EE587E heterozygotes, mirroring the genotype of Hoffman syndrome patients, had reduced spleen-to-body ratio, reduced total serum IgG, significantly lower antigen-specific antibody titers after ovalbumin or Pneumovax-23 immunization, and reduced numbers of B cells at most stages of B-cell development in bone marrow and spleen, with reduced Pax5 and Foxo1 but unchanged Rag1 and E2A expression and normal Notch1 and Tcf1.
quotes: Top2bEE587E/EE587E homozygous mice were not viable, similar to Top2b−/− mice, but Top2b+/EE587E heterozygotes could be recovered, which mirror the genotype of the Hoffman syndrome patients (Supplementary Table 7).

(1) the spleen-to-body ratio was reduced (Fig. 5a); (2) total serum IgG was reduced (Fig. 5b); (3) immunization with ovalbumin or Pneumovax-23 generated significantly lower titers of antigen-specific antibody (Fig. 5c, d); and (4) flow cytometric immunophenotyping of the bone marrow and spleen demonstrated reduced numbers of B cells at most stages of B-cell development
However, pre-B cells from Top2b+/EE587E mice demonstrated reduced expression of the B cell-specific transcription factors Pax5 and Foxo1 (Fig. 5I, J).

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) compared Top2b+/EE587E knockin to Top2b+/- mice and found that, similar to patient proband A, Top2b+/EE587E mice had decreased peripheral blood B cells that were reduced even compared with Top2b+/- mice without an effect on peripheral blood T cells, and had reduced KRECs with unaffected TRECs, supporting a dominant negative rather than purely haploinsufficient mechanism; splenic B cells from Top2b+/EE587E mice also showed increased DNA strand breaks by comet assay while T cells were unaffected.
quotes: Similar to patient proband A, Top2b+/EE587E mice had decreased peripheral blood B cells, which were reduced even compared to Top2b+/− mice, without an effect on peripheral blood T cells (Fig. 6a, b). In addition, KRECs were reduced in the Top2b+/EE587E mice, while T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) were unaffected (Fig. 6c, d)

Splenic B cells isolated from Top2b+/EE587E mice had increased DNA breaks compared to B cells from Top2b−/− mb1 cre and wild-type mice as measured by the increase in comet tail length (Fig. 6e, f), while the comet tail length was not altered in T cells derived from Top2b mutants (Fig. 6g).

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) found that B cells from Top2b+/EE587E mice stimulated in vitro with LPS with or without IL-4 secreted less total IgG, IgG3 and IgG2b than littermate controls, were reduced in number with greater LDH release, and more than 90% failed to advance beyond the first division after 5 days, whereas splenic T cells produced normal IL-2 in response to PMA and ionomycin and proliferated normally, consistent with the normal T-cell mitogen responses in patients.
quotes: In response to in vitro stimulation with LPS with or without IL-4, Top2b+/EE587E derived B cells demonstrated decreased secretion of total IgG, IgG3, and IgG2b compared to littermate controls (Fig. 7a, Supplementary Fig. 7a, b). In contrast, in vitro stimulation of isolated splenic T cells showed similar IL-2 production in response to PMA and ionomycin in both Top2b+/EE587E mice and controls (Fig. 7b).

After 5 days in culture, the majority of viable wild-type B cells had undergone 3–4 rounds of division, while more than 90% of mutant B cells did not advance beyond the first division (Fig. 7c, Supplementary Fig 7d.)

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) showed that wild-type mouse B cells have greater expression of Top2b mRNA and protein than T cells, consistent with previous reports in humans and mice, and proposed that the B cell-specific vulnerability reflects preferential reduction of long gene transcription when topoisomerases are absent, noting that murine B-cell transcription factor genes are longer (EBF 390 kb, Pax5 178 kb, Foxo1 85 kb) than T-cell (Tcf1 30 kb, Notch1 45 kb) or shared (Rag1 11 kb, E2A 24 kb) transcription factor genes; analysis of published Top2b ChIP-seq and END-seq data showed Top2b, but not Top2a, at the Pax5 promoter and intron 5 enhancer in murine primary B cells.
quotes: B cells have greater expression of Top2b mRNA and protein compared to T cells (Fig. 6h, i), which is consistent with previous reports in both humans and mice–. Together these results suggest that Top2b is more active in B cells than in T cells.

One possible explanation for this specificity is that long gene transcription is preferentially reduced when topoisomerases are absent or inhibited,, and that the murine B-cell transcription factors are notably longer (EBF is 390 kb, Pax5 is 178 kb, and Foxo1 is 85 kb) compared to T-cell transcription factors (Tcf1 is 30 kb and Notch1 is 45 kb)

Analysis of published Top2b ChIP-seq data and etoposide-induced DNA breaks as determined by END-seq from murine primary B cells showed the presence of Top2b (but not Top2a) in the promoter and enhancer (intron 5) regions of Pax5 (Supplementary Fig. 8).

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) noted that a brief clinical report had described a patient with progressive microcephaly, developmental delay, and hypotonia who had a TOP2B variant outside the TOPRIM domain (H58Y), but stated that no similarities to their patients were identified and that it was unclear whether that variant was causative.
quotes: Consistent with this latter possibility, a brief clinical report recently described a patient with progressive microcephaly, developmental delay, and hypotonia, who had a variant outside the TOPRIM domain of TOP2B (H58Y). However, no similarities to our patients were identified and it is currently unclear if this variant is causative.

findings.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) concluded that in three families with Hoffman syndrome three heterozygous mutations affecting the TOPRIM (DNA gating) domain of TOP2B were identified and that yeast studies indicated these were partially dominant loss-of-function mutations, consistent with the nonviability of homozygous Top2bEE587E/EE587E mice; inheritance in the families was autosomal dominant.
quotes: In three families with Hoffman syndrome,, we identified three heterozygous mutations affecting the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of the type II topoisomerase TOP2B. Introduction of these mutations into S. cerevisiae indicate that the mutations are partially dominant loss-of-function mutations, consistent with the nonviability of the homozygous Top2bEE587E/EE587E mice.
We previously reported two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology (Table 1, Supplementary Table 1),.

relevance_reason: The abstract describes a single sporadic patient with ablepharon-macrostomia syndrome and more significant hand and foot anomalies than previously reported. It does not mention B-cell immunodeficiency or BILU/Hoffman syndrome, so it gives only differential-diagnosis context for this entry.

findings.statement: Kallish et al. (2011) reported a sporadic patient with ablepharon-macrostomia syndrome and an expanded phenotype. The patient had more significant hand and foot anomalies than previously reported in that syndrome. The authors noted that ablepharon-macrostomia syndrome is characterized by absent or hypoplastic eyelids, fusion defects of the mouth, abnormal ears, ambiguous genitalia, skin differences, and developmental delay.
quotes: Here we present one additional sporadic case with an expanded phenotype. This patient has more significant hand and foot anomalies than previously reported.

characterized by absent or hypoplastic eyelids, fusion defects of the mouth with unfused lateral commissures, abnormal ears, ambiguous genitalia, skin differences including dry and coarse skin or redundant folds of skin, and developmental delay

relevance_reason: The paper reports new patients (a mother and her daughter) with Hoffman syndrome and reviews the clinical features of the disorder.

findings.statement: Hügle et al. (2011) reported a 7-year-old girl who had almost complete loss of B cells, facial dysmorphism, and malformations of the limbs and genitalia. Her mother had similar dysmorphic features and a milder form of the B-cell deficiency.
quotes: We report on a 7-year-old girl with almost complete loss of B cells, facial dysmorphism, and malformation of the limbs and genitalia, whose mother shows similar dysmorphic features with an attenuated version of the B-cell deficiency.

phenotypes.text: almost complete loss of B cells

findings.statement: Hügle et al. (2011) stated that Hoffman syndrome had originally been described as a sporadic case of humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies in a young girl. They believed that this case and their 2 patients had the same condition, and they reviewed the features of the 3 affected individuals.
quotes: One such report was a sporadic case of humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies in a young girl, later referred to as Hoffman syndrome.
We believe that all three cases described above represent the same condition.

relevance_reason: Reports a second family with BILU syndrome showing autosomal dominant inheritance, and excludes HOXA13 mutation or HOXA microdeletion.

findings.statement: Tischkowitz et al. (2004) reported a second family with B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities, genitourinary malformations, and mild dysmorphic features, similar to a previously described family. They further delineated the phenotype in females and concluded that this was a true syndromic association.
quotes: Here, we report a second family with similar features, which also shows autosomal dominant inheritance.
We further delineate the phenotype of this condition in females and add weight to the observation that this is a true syndromic association.

findings.statement: Tischkowitz et al. (2004) observed autosomal dominant inheritance in the second reported family with BILU syndrome, as in the first family.
quotes: Here, we report a second family with similar features, which also shows autosomal dominant inheritance.

findings.statement: In affected individuals from both reported BILU families, Tischkowitz et al. (2004) found no mutation in the candidate gene HOXA13 by sequence analysis and no evidence of a microdeletion involving HOXA13 or the HOXA cluster as a whole.
quotes: In affected individuals from both families, sequence analysis of candidate gene HOXA13 did not identify a mutation, and there was no evidence of a microdeletion involving either HOXA13 or the HOXA cluster as a whole.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a three-generation family with B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities and urogenital malformations, which is the defining report for this entry.

findings.statement: Edery et al. (2001) described a three-generation family with B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities, and urogenital malformations.
quotes: B cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities, and urogenital malformations in a three generation family

findings.statement: Edery et al. (2001) suggested that the disorder in their three-generation family might be a novel autosomal dominant syndrome.
quotes: a novel autosomal dominant syndrome?

relevance_reason: This is the original case report of the patient whose features define Hoffman (BILU) syndrome: humoral immunodeficiency with absent B cells, limb anomalies and urogenital/anal malformations.

findings.statement: Hoffman et al. (2001) reported a 6-year-old girl, one of a pair of twins, with isolated humoral immunodeficiency and a unique combination of dysmorphic features. These included microcephaly, micrognathia, sickle-shaped eyebrows, hypoplastic alae nasi, thenar hypoplasia, partial 4-5 toe syndactyly, recessed great toes, anterior anus, and hypoplastic labia minora. Radiographs showed triphalangeal thumbs and hypoplastic first metatarsals. She had postnatal growth retardation, and her development was substantially slower than her twin's.
quotes: We report a 6 year old girl with an isolated humoral immune deficiency and a unique combination of dysmorphic features.

Physical findings include microcephaly, micrognathia, sickle shaped eyebrows, hypoplastic alae nasi, thenar hypoplasia, partial 4-5 syndactyly of toes, recessed great toes, anterior anus, and hypoplastic labia minora.
Radiographic findings include triphalangeal thumbs and hypoplastic first metatarsals. She has postnatal growth retardation and her development is substantially slower than her twin's.

findings.statement: Hoffman et al. (2001) reported that the girl had recurrent sinopulmonary infections and pneumococcal bacteremia. Laboratory evaluation showed hypogammaglobulinemia and absent B cells.
quotes: Her clinical course has been complicated by recurrent sinopulmonary infections and pneumococcal bacteraemia.
Laboratory evaluation revealed hypogammaglobulinaemia, absent B cells, and a 46,XX karyotype.

findings.statement: Hoffman et al. (2001) found a normal 46,XX karyotype in the patient.
quotes: Laboratory evaluation revealed hypogammaglobulinaemia, absent B cells, and a 46,XX karyotype.

findings.statement: Hoffman et al. (2001) searched the literature and the London Dysmorphology Database and found no recognizable syndrome matching the patient's combination of features. They suggested that she may represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology.
quotes: A review of the literature and the London Dysmorphology Database did not produce any recognizable syndromes that match her constellation of findings.
She may represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology.
